sections.title: Identification
sections.text: Russula vesca has a variable cap colour, from wine-pink to buff, sometimes brownish or olive. In mature specimens the cap skin often stops short of the margin, leaving the pale gill tips visible as a fine line. The gills are white to very pale cream, fairly close, narrow and often forked near the stem. The stem is firm and white; the flesh is white with a mild, slightly nutty taste. Gills and stem may turn salmon to rusty pink when touched with iron salts.

sections.title: Habitat and caution
sections.text: This ectomycorrhizal species is common with beech and oak; on mainland Europe it is also reported under spruce on neutral to acidic soils. Fruiting season varies by region. It appears on recommended edible-mushroom lists, but cap colour alone is not enough for identification; any collection intended for eating must be identified with certainty.

traits: Cap 5 to 10 cm, initially globose then convex, sometimes with a shallow central depression; colour variable from wine-pink to buff, sometimes with brown, olive or green tints
The skin stops short of the margin, so the gills "show their teeth"
Gills white to very pale cream, fairly close and narrow, forked near the stem
Firm white stem, 3 to 10 cm tall and 1.5 to 2.5 cm wide
Firm white flesh, mild taste with a nutty note
Mycorrhizal, especially with beech and oak; also reported with spruce in mainland Europe, on neutral to acidic soils · July to October (season varies by region)
The gills and stem react to ferrous sulfate, turning salmon to rusty pink
safetyNote: Edible and included in the DGfM and VAPKO recommended mushroom lists. As with any russula, eat only after certain identification; cap colour is highly variable and is not sufficient on its own to identify this species.
